title: signal 4 on freebsd arm64 due to missing cache synchronisation
body: On FreeBSD ARM64, running Firefox versions newer than 115 with content-process write protection disabled, using W+X pages without an mprotect call between writing and executing JIT code, kills Firefox with signal 4. JIT code should be ready to execute. The ARM64 cache synchronization code in MozCpu-vixl.cpp should also run when __FreeBSD__ is defined; the related FreeBSD investigation is linked.

symptoms_visible: On FreeBSD ARM64, JIT code in Firefox versions newer than 115 kills Firefox with signal 4 when content-process code write protection is off and no mprotect call occurs between writing and executing the code.
N0.label: N0 FreeBSD ARM64 JIT signal reported

symptoms_visible: The unpatched FreeBSD ARM64 build still exits with signal 4 when it tries to execute JIT code under the W+X configuration.
N1.label: N1 unrelated MAP_FIXED issue separated

symptoms_visible: The original unpatched Firefox configuration still produces signal 4 on FreeBSD ARM64; I tested my cache-invalidation patch against Firefox 122 build2.
N2.label: N2 cache diagnosis confirmed and initial patch tested

symptoms_visible: Without the patch, FreeBSD ARM64 JIT execution still ends in signal 4 under the W+X configuration.
N3.label: N3 platform guards and final patch refined

symptoms_visible: On a Firefox build containing the fix, FreeBSD ARM64 JIT code executes without Firefox being killed by signal 4.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Is the MAP_FIXED change from the downstream patch also required to stop this JIT signal 4 crash?
Does the GC Memory.cpp MAP_FIXED change belong to the cache-invalidation fix?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. MAP_FIXED solves running with ASLR on FreeBSD and is another story I still have to investigate. It is unrelated to the JIT crash with signal 4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, the cache-invalidation change alone still gives signal 4; the crash stops only when I also apply the MAP_FIXED change.
I also use a different FreeBSD package build directory.

edges.comment: Comments 3 and 6 separate the downstream MAP_FIXED/ASLR work from the signal 4 cache-invalidation defect.

question_patterns: Can you submit the cache-invalidation patch and say which Firefox build you tested it against?
Which version have you been able to build and test with the proposed FreeBSD change?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached cacheinvalidation.patch. It is based on tip, but I have only tested it on Firefox 122 build2 because I do not have easy access to newer NSS on FreeBSD.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched source does not compile on FreeBSD ARM64, so I have not been able to run it.
I tested the same patch on a local Firefox 122 build from a slightly newer ports revision.

question_patterns: How does your patch handle native AArch64 operating systems that do not have an implemented cache-invalidation branch?
Does the patch also prevent an unrecognized AArch64 host from falling through to the simulator no-op?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I added FreeBSD to the cache synchronization path and used the suggested compile-time error for unsupported native ARM64 operating systems. I excluded OpenBSD from that error because its cache code is neither needed nor able to compile there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I only changed the misleading comment; FreeBSD still reaches the no-op branch.

solution.intent: Confirm the reporter's cache-coherency diagnosis and add FreeBSD ARM64 to the real instruction-cache invalidation path, while keeping the unrelated MAP_FIXED/ASLR issue out of this fix.
solution.concrete_example: Update MozCpu-vixl.cpp so native FreeBSD AArch64 executes the instruction-cache synchronization code after JIT code is written. The prior mprotect transitions had masked the missing invalidation; MAP_FIXED is a separate FreeBSD ASLR issue.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the W+X/no-mprotect behavior and proposed FreeBSD cache synchronization. The explanation that earlier mprotect transitions had been masking stale ARM instruction-cache contents was confirmed by the JavaScript engine developer.

edges.comment: Comments 3, 6, and 8 confirm the diagnosis, preserve the separation from MAP_FIXED, and provide the initial upstream patch and its raw test scope. The attached patch is not available as a local benchmark image.

question_patterns: Why is OpenBSD excluded from the new instruction-cache invalidation requirement?
Why would OpenBSD ARM64 not need the same explicit cache invalidation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: OpenBSD always write-protects JIT code, so I assume its mprotect behaves the same way with regard to the cache; otherwise they would have seen the same issue. I do not currently have an ARM64 OpenBSD machine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I tested OpenBSD ARM64 with write protection disabled and it also crashes with signal 4 unless the same cache invalidation is enabled.

question_patterns: How did you revise the platform handling in CPU::GetCacheType()?
Does the final patch also emit the unsupported-OS compile error from GetCacheType?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I first attached cacheinvalidation2.patch using the same strategy for CPU::GetCacheType(), then attached cacheinvalidation3.patch so GetCacheType does not error out.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I made the same final adjustment in one amended patch instead of uploading a third revision.

edges.comment: Comments 10-12, 17, and 18 discuss OpenBSD and record the reporter's final patch revisions.

solution.intent: Land the refined FreeBSD ARM64 instruction-cache invalidation fix, prevent unsupported native ARM64 systems from silently using the simulator no-op path, and have the reporter verify a build containing the fix before treating the signal 4 crash as resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Land the MozCpu-vixl.cpp change that uses instruction-cache invalidation on FreeBSD ARM64 and guards unhandled native AArch64 platforms from the simulator no-op path (mozilla-central revision 1b595199c4de), while retaining the final GetCacheType behavior. Then ask the reporter to retest an affected JIT workload in a current build and confirm that signal 4 no longer occurs.
solution.inference_hint: The complete root-cause chain combines the reporter's FreeBSD ARM64 W+X observations with engineer analysis: bug 1672619's OpenBSD-oriented preprocessor change omitted cache invalidation on other unlisted native ARM64 systems, while the later move away from content-process W^X removed the mprotect transitions that had hidden the defect.

edges.comment: Comment 7 identifies the OpenBSD-ifdef regression. The refined fix landed on autoland and mozilla-central as revision 1b595199c4de. Beta uplift coordination is intentionally not scored; the technical resolution is the FreeBSD ARM64 cache-invalidation change plus verification that the signal is gone.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: FreeBSD native ARM64 fell outside the implemented JIT instruction-cache invalidation branches, leaving stale instructions after generated code was written; the later W+X behavior exposed the defect because mprotect transitions no longer masked it.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the FreeBSD ARM64 signal 4 behavior, the W+X/no-mprotect condition, the affected platform conditionals, and the reporter's patch testing.
Must fix MozCpu-vixl.cpp so FreeBSD ARM64 executes instruction-cache invalidation and must avoid silently treating an unsupported native AArch64 host as a simulator.
Must not present the downstream MAP_FIXED/ASLR change as the fix for this signal 4 crash; the reporter explicitly identified it as a separate issue.
Must ask the reporter to retest an affected JIT workload on a build containing the fix and must not declare resolution until Firefox executes the JIT code without signal 4.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical FreeBSD maintainer and Firefox porter who can analyze ARM64 JIT memory behavior, read and modify platform preprocessor code, build Firefox, and author upstream patches.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, concise, and implementation-focused; supplies exact source locations and downstream investigation links, distinguishes unrelated platform issues, and iterates patches in response to review.
